newsitem.title: UK: Russia's rating to be reviewed later this year-S&P.
newsitem.headline: Russia's rating to be reviewed later this year-S&P.

text.p: Russia's credit assessment by U.S. rating agency Standard & Poor's will come up for its annual review fairly soon, S&P director Konrad Reuss said on Friday, although he could not specify a date.
"A review of Russia is coming up at some point in the near future," Reuss told Reuters.

He was commenting on market speculation in Moscow on Friday that Russia would not be upgraded from its current BB minus rating. Previously there was market talk in London that Russia might be due for an upgrade.
The BB minus rating on Russia's long-term foreign currency debt was assigned in October 1996 with a stable outlook.
Reuss said the latest rumours could have been triggered by the fact that Russia was coming up for its annual rating review.

"What that review will reveal is hard to say at this point," he said. "Every rating decision is the decision of a credit committee and it has to be discussed. Therefore it is impossible to say what will happen later this year."
"Normally we would not make any pre-announcement about any possible rating action, or specify a month when we would expect any rating action."
Reuss said the standard procedure was to review a credit on a routine basis once a year, unless otherwise warranted.
